output.summary: A perennial herb native to the eastern and central United States, violet woodsorrel grows from an underground bulb and has three heart-shaped leaflets and lavender-to-white spring flowers. All parts are edible and used in salads, but only moderate amounts are advised because its oxalic acid can be poisonous in large quantities.
output.edibilityNote: Flowers, leaves, stems and bulbs are edible and traditionally eaten, including in salads, but large quantities may be poisonous because of oxalic acid.
